facts: Today is the hundredth birthday fair of the town of Brackenford.
The clock in the old clock tower on the town square has stopped. Its hands point at ten past six.
The clock's brass winding key is missing from its hook inside the tower.
Without the brass winding key, nobody can wind the clock and start it again, so it cannot strike noon.
For a hundred years the birthday fair has opened when the tower clock strikes noon.
At quarter past seven Mayor Pike noticed the clock still said ten past six. Mr. Finch, the clockkeeper, climbed up and found the key hook empty.
People are getting the fair ready across the town square, the clock tower, the bakery, the bandstand, the library and the river path.

timeline: Friday afternoon: Marigold Vane leaves the town band's music folder on the bandstand, and the rain soaks it. Later she grumbles to Mayor Pike that the clock's noon bongs drown out the band's Birthday March.

Saturday 5:10am: Mr. Finch unlocks the tower door's padlock and climbs to the clock room. At 5:20 he winds the clock full with the brass winding key and hangs the key back on its hook by the clock room door. The clock is ticking and right.

5:20am to 5:40am: Nell Ashby slips in at the open tower door and climbs the belfry ladder to watch the barn owl. She notes it on a page torn from her bird-spotting notebook. At 5:40 Mr. Finch spots her and shoos her down, and in her hurry she drops the torn page on the ladder. She runs home to the library, arriving at 5:45, and stays there helping her mum until seven.
5:45am: Mayor Pike starts hanging bunting on the town square from a ladder.
5:50am: Mr. Finch hurries to the jetty on the river path to meet the supply boat bringing the fair's bunting. In his hurry he forgets to lock the tower door's padlock.

5:55am to 6:25am: Mr. Finch carries the bunting boxes off the supply boat at the jetty, one by one, in Ollie Brook's sight the whole time. The boatman writes the time beside each box on the delivery slip as Mr. Finch carries it ashore, and Mr. Finch signs the slip at 6:20.
6:00am: Marigold Vane arrives at the library and copies new band music on the photocopier until 6:40, with Rosa and Nell Ashby there. Nobody is at the bandstand.

6:00am: the tower clock strikes six. Ben Crumb, the baker's son, brings the bakery's rolls to the jetty. Ollie Brook tells him the Lowmill ferry has broken a paddle and will not arrive until one o'clock. Ben's great-gran, Granny Bea, is on that ferry.
6:02am: Ben runs up Tower Lane towards the clock tower with his bread basket, wearing his floury Comet trainers with a star on each heel.
6:07am: Mayor Pike, up her ladder, sees a child with a bread basket slip in at the tower door, but bunting hides who it is.

6:10am: in the clock room Ben holds the pendulum still with his floury hands, so the clock stops at ten past six. He takes the brass winding key off its hook, so nobody can start the clock before Granny Bea arrives. His floury trainers leave star-heel prints on the dusty stairs.
6:13am: Ben runs out of the tower, dropping a bakery roll on the bottom step. The quarter-past chime never comes.
6:20am: back at the bakery, Ben hides the brass key in the blue tin on the top shelf. At 6:30 he leaves the band's rolls on the empty bandstand.
7:15am: Mayor Pike notices the clock still says ten past six. Mr. Finch climbs up and finds the key hook empty and the tower door unlocked.

After 7:15am: Ben tells everyone he was helping Ms. Vane set out chairs at the bandstand at ten past six, and blames Mr. Finch. Ms. Vane says she was at the bandstand all morning. Mrs. Ashby says Nell never left the library. Nell says she has never been up the tower. Mr. Finch says he locked the door.
truth.motive: Ben's great-gran, Granny Bea, pulled the bell rope for noon at the town's fiftieth birthday fair, and all year she has said she wants to hear the clock strike noon at the hundredth. When Ben heard her ferry would not arrive until one o'clock, he stopped the clock and hid the key so that noon would wait for her. He meant to give the key back when she arrived, but he got scared of getting into trouble and blamed Mr. Finch instead.

town_square.name: The Town Square
facts: The town square is busy with people putting up stalls and strings of bunting.
The old clock tower stands at one corner of the square, its hands stuck at ten past six.
A huge birthday cake waits on a table under a striped awning.

clock_tower.name: The Clock Tower
facts: The clock tower is cool and dusty inside, and it smells of old wood and oil.
Narrow wooden stairs climb up to the clock room, where the great clock's gears and pendulum hang.
Above the clock room, a ladder leads up into the belfry.

bakery.name: Crumb's Bakery
facts: Crumb's Bakery is warm and smells of fresh bread.
Flour dusts the counter, the floor and the shelves.
Shelves of tins and jars rise all the way up to the ceiling.

spots.name: the blue tin on the top shelf

bandstand.name: The Bandstand
facts: The bandstand is a round, green-roofed stage in the park beside the square.
A basket of bakery rolls sits on its steps.
Instrument cases and music stands are lined up at the back.

library.name: The Library
facts: The library is quiet, with tall bookshelves and a squashy window seat.
Boxes of old books are packed for the fair's book stall.
A photocopier hums in the corner.

river_path.name: The River Path
facts: The river path runs along the water to a little wooden jetty.
Ducks paddle by the jetty posts.
Tower Lane leads up from the jetty towards the clock tower, and the path itself runs on towards the park and the bandstand.

mayor_pike.name: Mayor Edna Pike
mayor_pike.personality: Brisk, cheerful and a little bossy, with a clipboard for everything. She is worried the fair will be spoiled but tries to stay jolly.

demeanor.open: Busy and flustered but glad of help. She talks quickly and checks her clipboard between answers.

knows.fact: Mayor Pike has been mayor of Brackenford for twelve years.
The giant birthday cake will be cut at the first strike of noon.
The town band plays the Birthday March after the noon chime.

appearance: Mayor Pike is a tall woman with silver hair in a bun.
She wears a gold mayor's chain over a bright red coat.

finch.name: Mr. Hector Finch
finch.personality: Gruff, proud and old-fashioned, the clockkeeper for thirty years. He loves the clock and hates to admit a mistake.

demeanor.guarded: Stiff and touchy. He is offended anyone could think he would harm his own clock, and he keeps glancing at the tower door.
demeanor.shaken: Red-faced and grumbling at himself. He knows his mistake let somebody in.
demeanor.cleared: Relieved and gruffly kind. He just wants his key back and his clock ticking.

knows.fact: Mr. Finch has wound the tower clock every morning for thirty years.
The clock is wound once a day, and it chimes every quarter of an hour.
The town band practises at the bandstand in the park.

appearance: Mr. Finch is an old man with a bushy white beard.
He wears a brown waistcoat with a watch chain and big work boots.

ben.name: Ben Crumb
ben.personality: A friendly, eager eleven-year-old who loves his great-gran. He is normally honest, so lying makes him chatty, fidgety and too helpful.

demeanor.guarded: Over-friendly and quick to answer, offering buns. He keeps steering the talk to Mr. Finch.
demeanor.shaken: Quieter. He stops offering buns and keeps looking out of the window at the river.
demeanor.cornered: Close to tears, staring at his floury trainers.
demeanor.cleared: Tearful but relieved. He wants to say sorry to Mr. Finch and explain about Granny Bea.

knows.fact: Ben's mum, Mrs. Crumb, baked the giant birthday cake for the fair.
Ben helps with the bakery's deliveries on Saturday mornings.

appearance: Ben is a boy with sticky-up ginger hair and freckles.
He wears a flour-dusted apron over a blue jumper, and bright trainers.

marigold.name: Ms. Marigold Vane
marigold.personality: Dramatic, proud and loud, the leader of the town band. She hates to look foolish in front of her band.

demeanor.guarded: Grand and a bit too loud. She waves her baton about and talks over awkward questions.
demeanor.shaken: Embarrassed and pink, fiddling with her baton.
demeanor.cleared: Sheepish, then warm. She laughs at herself and offers to help find the key.

knows.fact: Marigold Vane has led the Brackenford town band for ten years.
The band has been practising the Birthday March for weeks.

appearance: Ms. Vane is a woman with a cloud of curly red hair.
She wears a band jacket with shiny gold buttons and carries a baton.

rosa.name: Mrs. Rosa Ashby
rosa.personality: Gentle, careful and protective of her daughter. She tells the truth about books and times, but she will fib to keep Nell out of trouble.

demeanor.open: Kind and soft-spoken, glad to help.
demeanor.guarded: Polite but tight-lipped whenever Nell comes up. She tidies things that are already tidy.
demeanor.cleared: Apologetic and honest. She wants Nell treated fairly.

knows.fact: Mrs. Ashby runs the library and lives in the flat above it with her daughter Nell.
The library is running a second-hand book stall at the fair.

appearance: Mrs. Ashby is a woman with glasses on a beaded chain.
She wears a long green cardigan with pencils in the pocket.

nell.name: Nell Ashby
nell.personality: A quiet, clever eleven-year-old who loves birds and facts. She hates breaking rules and goes very still when she is worried.

demeanor.guarded: Quiet and careful. She answers in short sentences and hugs her notebook.
demeanor.shaken: Pink-cheeked and worried, sure she is in big trouble.
demeanor.cleared: Relieved and suddenly chatty, full of facts about owls.

knows.fact: Nell is in the same class at school as Ben Crumb.
Nell has helped at the library every Saturday since she was seven.

appearance: Nell is a girl with two long dark plaits.
She wears a yellow raincoat and carries a small notebook.

ollie.name: Mr. Ollie Brook
ollie.personality: Easy-going, kind and chatty, the jetty keeper. He notices boats and people and likes a good natter.

demeanor.open: Relaxed and friendly, leaning on a jetty post. He is happy to chat.

knows.fact: Ollie Brook has looked after the Brackenford jetty for twenty years.
Ollie eats a Crumb's Bakery roll for breakfast every morning.

appearance: Mr. Brook is a round man with a woolly hat and a grey moustache.
He wears tall rubber boots and a yellow life jacket.

ev_pendulum.fact: The clock's weights are still wound up nearly to the top, so the clock did not run down. The pendulum hangs dead still, and its brass bob has small floury finger marks on it. Someone stopped the clock by hand at ten past six.

ev_flour_prints.fact: Small floury footprints, the size of a child's shoe, go up the dusty tower stairs to the clock room and back down. Each print has a zigzag tread with a little star pressed into the heel.

ev_open_padlock.fact: The tower door's padlock hangs open on its hook. It is not broken or scratched, so nobody forced it: the tower door was left unlocked this morning.

ev_empty_hook.fact: The hook by the clock room door is empty. A clean outline in the dust on the wall shows where the big brass winding key usually hangs.

ev_dropped_roll.fact: A fresh bread roll with Crumb's Bakery's red paper band lies on the bottom step of the clock tower stairs.

ev_owl_note.fact: On the belfry ladder lies a page torn from a bird-spotting notebook. It says: 'Barn owl in the tower belfry, 5:30am. N.A.' Small muddy welly prints go up and down the ladder rungs.

ev_delivery_list.fact: A delivery list in Mrs. Crumb's writing is pinned by the counter: 'Saturday. Ben: 6:00am rolls to the jetty for Mr. Brook. 6:30am rolls to the band at the bandstand.'

ev_ovens.fact: The bread ovens are still warm from the night's baking of the giant birthday cake.

ev_key_in_tin.fact: Inside the blue tin on the bakery's top shelf, under a pile of paper doilies, is the clock tower's big brass winding key, dusted with flour.

source.spot: the blue tin on the top shelf

ev_chairs.fact: The bandstand chairs are still stacked in a tall pile under a tarpaulin, and the morning dew on the tarpaulin is unbroken. Nobody has set out any chairs this morning.

ev_horns.fact: The brass horns in their cases are dull and smudged with old fingerprints, and the polishing cloth is folded and dry. Nobody has polished the horns this morning.

ev_empty_stands.fact: The music stands are bare. A note taped to one says: 'Band music folder soaked in Friday's rain. New copies coming. M.V.'

ev_copier.fact: A forgotten page of band music, 'Brackenford Birthday March', sits in the library photocopier's tray. The copier's slip says 60 copies were made between 6:02am and 6:38am this morning.

ev_visitors_book.fact: The library visitors' book has one entry for this morning: 'Marigold Vane. In 6:00am, copying band music. Out 6:40am.'

ev_window_seat.fact: A bird book lies open on the library window seat at a page about barn owls.

ev_ferry_notice.fact: A chalk notice on the jetty noticeboard says: 'Lowmill ferry: broken paddle. Will now arrive at 1 o'clock. Sorry! Posted 6am.'

ev_bunting_slip.fact: A delivery slip tucked in the bunting boxes lists 12 boxes of fair bunting. Beside each box the boatman has written the time Mr. Finch carried it ashore at the jetty, one box every two or three minutes: box 1 at 5:55am, box 7 at 6:10am, box 12 at 6:20am. At the bottom: 'Received by H. Finch, 6:20am.' So Mr. Finch was at the jetty, carrying boxes, at ten past six.

ev_cake_table.fact: A sign on the cake table says: 'Brackenford's 100th Birthday Cake. To be cut at the first strike of noon.'

mayor_chimes.fact: Mayor Pike says she was up her ladder hanging bunting on the square from quarter to six. She heard the tower clock strike six o'clock, but the quarter-past chime never came.

mayor_grumble.fact: Mayor Pike says that yesterday Ms. Vane, the bandleader, complained that the clock's noon bongs drown out the band's Birthday March, and said she wished the old clock would be quiet for once.

mayor_tower_door.fact: Mayor Pike remembers that at about seven minutes past six, from her ladder, she saw a child carrying a bread basket slip in at the tower door. Bunting hid the child's face, so she could not see who it was.

finch_wound.fact: Mr. Finch says he wound the clock full with the brass winding key at twenty past five this morning, and hung the key back on its hook by the clock room door. The clock was ticking and right when he left the tower at ten to six.

finch_locked.fact: Mr. Finch says he locked the tower door's padlock behind him when he left at ten to six, so nobody could have got in.
finch_locked.why: He forgot to lock it in his hurry to meet the bunting boat, and he is too proud to admit his mistake let someone in.

tell_finch_pocket.fact: Mr. Finch pats his waistcoat pocket, where the padlock key clinks, and his eyes slide away towards the tower door.

finch_shooed_nell.fact: Mr. Finch says that at twenty to six he found Nell Ashby, the librarian's daughter, up the belfry ladder watching the barn owl, and shooed her home. She left before he did, and the key was still on its hook.

reached.about: anyone else in the tower this morning

finch_admits_unlocked.fact: Mr. Finch admits he forgot to lock the tower door at ten to six because he was hurrying to the jetty to meet the boat bringing the fair's bunting. He was at the jetty unloading boxes until twenty-five past six.

line.text: They ask Mr. Finch whether he really clicked the padlock shut, or what he was hurrying off to do.

ollie_finch_jetty.fact: Ollie Brook says Mr. Finch was at the jetty from five to six until twenty-five past six, unloading the fair's bunting boxes, and never once left his sight.

ollie_ben_rolls.fact: Ollie Brook says Ben Crumb brought the bakery rolls to the jetty at six o'clock. Ollie told him the Lowmill ferry had broken a paddle and would not arrive until one o'clock. Ben went pale and said, 'But Granny Bea is on it!'

reached.about: who came to the jetty this morning

ollie_ben_ran.fact: Ollie Brook says that when Ben left the jetty at two minutes past six, he did not go along the river path towards the bandstand. He ran up Tower Lane towards the clock tower, with his bread basket bouncing on his arm.

ollie_granny.fact: Ollie Brook says Granny Bea is Ben's great-gran. Fifty years ago, as a girl, she pulled the bell rope for noon at the town's fiftieth birthday fair, and all year she has said she wants to hear the clock strike noon at the hundredth.

ben_alibi.fact: Ben Crumb says that after taking the rolls to the jetty, he went straight along the river path to the bandstand and helped Ms. Vane set out the chairs at ten past six. He says he never went near the clock tower.
ben_alibi.why: He was in the clock tower at ten past six stopping the clock, and he heard that Ms. Vane was at the bandstand all morning.

ben_blames_finch.fact: Ben Crumb says Mr. Finch must have done it, because it is his key and he was the only one in the tower this morning.
ben_blames_finch.why: He wants everyone looking at Mr. Finch instead of at him.

tell_ben_star.fact: When Ben hops off his stool, his floury trainers leave a print on the bakery floor: a zigzag tread with a little star pressed into the heel. He quickly scuffs it away with his foot.

tell_ben_tin.fact: While he talks about the bandstand, Ben keeps glancing up at the blue tin on the bakery's top shelf, then quickly looks away.

tell_ben_granny.fact: When Granny Bea or the late ferry comes up, Ben's eyes go shiny and he stares out of the bakery window towards the river.

reached.subject: Granny Bea or the late Lowmill ferry

ben_no_key.fact: Ben Crumb says he has not seen the brass winding key and has never been up the clock tower.
ben_no_key.why: He took the key himself and hid it in the bakery.

ben_drops_blame.fact: Ben Crumb admits Mr. Finch could not have done it: when Ben took the rolls to the jetty at six o'clock, Mr. Finch was there unloading bunting boxes.

ben_granny_wish.fact: Ben Crumb says Granny Bea is on the late Lowmill ferry and won't arrive until one o'clock. He says it isn't fair if the clock strikes noon without her, when she has waited fifty years to hear it.

line.text: They ask Ben gently about Granny Bea and whether she will be here to see the fair open.

ben_confession.fact: Ben Crumb admits that at six o'clock he heard Granny Bea's ferry would be late. He ran up Tower Lane, found the tower door open, climbed to the clock room, held the pendulum still at ten past six and took the brass winding key, so the clock could not strike noon before Granny Bea arrived. He hid the key in the blue tin on the bakery's top shelf and meant to give it back when she came.

marigold_alibi.fact: Ms. Vane says she was at the bandstand from half past five until seven o'clock this morning, polishing the band's horns, and she saw nobody else there.
marigold_alibi.why: She left the band's music folder out in Friday's rain and spent the morning secretly copying new music at the library. She does not want the band to know she ruined their music.

tell_marigold_fingers.fact: Ms. Vane tucks her hands behind her back, but her fingertips are smudged grey, like photocopier ink.

marigold_grumble.fact: Ms. Vane admits she grumbled that the clock's noon bongs drown out the band's Birthday March, but says she would never stop the town's clock on its hundredth birthday.

reached.about: her complaint about the clock's bongs

marigold_library_truth.fact: Ms. Vane admits she was not at the bandstand at all this morning. She left the band's music folder out on the bandstand on Friday and the rain ruined it, and she did not want the band to know, so she pretended she had been at the bandstand. From six o'clock until twenty to seven she was in the library copying new band music, with Mrs. Ashby and Nell Ashby there the whole time. Nobody set out chairs, and she has not seen Ben Crumb at all today.

line.text: They ask Ms. Vane about the grey smudges on her fingers.

rosa_nell_lie.fact: Mrs. Ashby says Nell has been with her in the library since five o'clock this morning and never went near the clock tower.
rosa_nell_lie.why: She knows Nell sneaks up the tower to watch the owl, and she wants to keep Nell out of trouble.

tell_rosa_wellies.fact: Mrs. Ashby straightens the same pile of books twice and glances at Nell's muddy wellies by the library door.

rosa_nell_truth.fact: Mrs. Ashby admits Nell slipped out at quarter past five to watch the barn owl in the tower belfry and came home at quarter to six. From quarter to six until seven, Nell was right here in the library helping with the photocopier, including at ten past six.

line.text: They ask Mrs. Ashby kindly about Nell's muddy wellies by the door.

rosa_marigold.fact: Mrs. Ashby says Ms. Vane was in the library from six o'clock until twenty to seven this morning, copying band music on the photocopier.

reached.about: who else came to the library this morning

nell_never_tower.fact: Nell Ashby says she has never been up the clock tower, because children are not allowed.
nell_never_tower.why: She climbed the belfry ladder early this morning to watch the barn owl and is scared of getting into trouble.

tell_nell_feather.fact: A soft white-and-gold owl feather pokes out of Nell's bird-spotting notebook, which has a page torn out. She closes the notebook quickly.

nell_owl_truth.fact: Nell Ashby admits she slipped into the tower at twenty past five and climbed the belfry ladder to watch the barn owl. She wrote the owl down on a page torn from her notebook, signed with her initials N.A., and dropped it on the ladder when Mr. Finch shooed her home at twenty to six. She never touched the clock, and she was back in the library by quarter to six.

line.text: They ask Nell about the owl feather and the torn-out page in her notebook.

nell_comet.fact: Nell Ashby says trainers with a zigzag tread and a star pressed into each heel are Comet trainers. Ben Crumb is the only child in Brackenford who has a pair: his Granny Bea sent them from the city for his birthday.

reached.about: trainers with a star on the heel

stop_time.text: The clock did not run down: someone stopped it by hand at ten past six, so whoever took the key was in the clock tower at ten past six.

finch_cleared.text: Mr. Finch is cleared: at ten past six he was at the jetty on the river path, unloading bunting.

nell_alibi_early.text: Nell was in the library with her mum all morning, so she cannot have stopped the clock.

nell_cleared.text: Nell is cleared: whatever she did earlier, at ten past six she was in the library.

marigold_cleared.text: Ms. Vane is cleared: at ten past six she was in the library copying band music.

door_explained.text: The tower door was open because Mr. Finch forgot to lock it when he hurried to the jetty, not because he let anyone in on purpose.
door_explained.resolves: red herring: the unlocked tower door

owl_explained.text: The torn notebook page signed N.A. and the small muddy welly prints on the belfry ladder are Nell's, left when she watched the barn owl before six.
owl_explained.resolves: red herring: the owl-watcher in the belfry

grumble_explained.text: Ms. Vane grumbled about the clock's bongs, and lied about the bandstand only to hide that she ruined the band's music.
grumble_explained.resolves: red herring: the bandleader who wanted the clock quiet

culprit_ben.text: Ben Crumb stopped the clock by hand at ten past six and took the brass winding key.

motive.text: Ben wanted noon to wait for his great-gran, Granny Bea, whose ferry would not arrive until one o'clock.
